bibl.author: P. Ovidius Naso
bibl.title: P. Ovidii Nasonis operum tomus primus
bibl.ref: Washington and Lee University Special Collections, PA6519 .A2 1751, volume 1
bibl.note: One-based viewer images 177–178; printed page numbers are 44 lower. Archive page labels differ from both. The actual images, rather than another witness or uncorrected OCR, supply the readings.

normalization.p: Source spelling, capitalization, punctuation, written ampersands and visible accents are retained. Long s and typographic ligatures are represented by standard s and constituent letters. Letter spacing in display capitals and quotation glyph shapes may be represented schematically. No modern-edition readings are substituted.

segmentation.p: Each l represents one canonical verse, with stable numbering and a link to its existing image region. Source verse order and headings are retained. Couplet grouping and canonical line numbers are editorial. A displaced word may remain within its verse with its position marked.

Compared actual line starts on each full-page image, including at page transitions. This setting uses a recurring couplet inset; the explicit list records the observed inset starts in this poem, not a rule inferred from verse-number parity. Initial capitals and drop capitals vary the apparent left edge.

correction.p: Uncertain readings remain locally marked with unclear or gap. Observations and uncertainties are documented for a different source reader; ink colour alone does not establish erasure or a separate hand.

revisionDesc.change: First reader inspected and transcribed all 48 verses from the source images; independent source review pending.

Independent reviewer inspected every extant verse in full-page context and enlarged source-image bands, corrected source readings and page furniture, and checked observed line starts. Review report and exact XML/report hashes are recorded in the companion ledger.

Fresh corpus source reading rechecked all 48 verses, every evidence note, headings, page furniture and full-page line starts. No further verse wording changes were supported. Prior independent second-pass history is retained; changed readings were additionally corroborated from native crops by /root/w_review_c. See W-3.4-second-pass.md.

lg.label: Elegia IV. Ad virum servantem conjugem.
lg.l: DUre vir, imposito tenerae custode puellae,
Nil agis. ingenio quaeque tuenda suo.
Si qua metu dempto casta est; ea denique casta est:
Quae, quia non liceat, non facit, illa facit.
Ut jam servaris bene corpus; adultera mens est:
Nec custodiri, ni velit, illa potest.
Nec mentem servare potes, licet omnia claudas.
Omnibus occlusis intus adulter erit.
Cui peccare licet, peccat minus. ipsa potestas
Semina nequitiae languidiora facit.
Desine (crede mihi) vitia irritare vetando:
Obsequio vincas aptius illa tuo.
Vidi ego nuper equum, contra sua vincla tenacem,
Ore reluctanti fulminis ire modo
Constitit, ut primum concessas sensit habenas,
Frenaque in effusâ laxa jacere jubâ.
Nitimur in vetitum semper, cupimusque negata.
Sic interdictis imminet aeger aquis.
Centum fronte oculos, centum cervice gerebat
Argus: & hos unus saepe fefellit Amor.
In thalamum Danaë saxo ferroque perennem
Quae fuerat virgo tradita, mater erat.
Penelope mansit, quamvis custode carebat,
Inter tot juvenes intemerata procos.
Quidquid servatur, cupimus magis: ipsaque furem
Cura vocat. pauci, quod sinit alter, amant.
Nec facie placet illa suâ, sed amore mariti.
Nescio quid, quod te ceperit, esse putant.
Non proba sit, quam vir servat, sed adultera. cara est;
Ipse timor pretium corpore majus habet.
Indignere licet; juvat inconcessa voluptas.
Sola placet; Timeo, dicere si qua potest.
Nec tamen ingenuam jus est servare puellam.
Hic metus externae corpora gentis agat.
Scilicet ut possit custos, Ego, dicere, feci,
In laudem servi casta sit illa tui.
Rusticus est nimium, quem laedit adultera conjux;
Et notos mores non satis Urbis habet:
In quâ Martigenae non sunt sine crimine nati
Romulus Iliades, Iliadesque Remus.
Quo tibi formosam, si non nisi casta placebat?
Non possunt ullis ista coire modis.
Si sapis, indulge dominae; vultusque severos
Exsue: nec rigidi jura tuere viri.
Et cole, quos dederit (multos dabit) uxor amicos.
Gratia sic minimo magna labore venit.
Sic poteris juvenum convivia semper inire:
Et, quae non dederis, multa videre domi.

div.head: Transcription notes
div.note: The poem heading and its italic descriptive title are printed immediately before the first verse; the title is retained as source metadata rather than verse text.

Verse 2 begins beside the two-line initial, approximately three character widths farther right than the ordinary inset verse starts. The additional opening space is based on the actual full-page line starts.
